messages:
maya: quick heads up — observed a KV cache memory growth regression on Dedicated pool d-4 compared to Hosted and Private during long-context workloads. +700MB over baseline after ~10k tokens :thinking:
alex: ah ok. is this the long-chat benchmark or something synthetic?
maya: long-chat (user sessions ~20k tokens). repro steps below. reproduction is reliable on d-4 with current released runtime (v1.24.0). Hosted runs same model/config and stays ~+40MB, Private (onprem) oscillates but not as bad.
jin: any config drift between pools? page thresholds, batch/window sizes?
maya:yeah — found differences: Dedicated has `kv.page_threshold=0.6`, Hosted `kv.page_threshold=0.85`, Private `kv.page_threshold=0.55` (customer override). Also Dedicated uses kernel huts: `sched` tunables differ (hosted tuned by infra).
sam: interesting — lower page_threshold should evict earlier so less growth, but you're seeing more growth on Dedicated (threshold=0.6). maybe eviction is failing or fragmentation prevents reuse.
maya: from `pmap` and our allocator traces: resident increases monotonically, but free slab count is non-zero. fragmentation high: many small free spans. sample dump:
```
KVAllocator: total=16GB resident=14.9GB free_spans=18 small_spans=1024 fragmented_bytes=720MB
evict_attempts=240 evict_success=16
pager_faults=412
```
jin: evict_success 16 / 240 is way too low. looks like eviction scanning isn't finding reusable frames — maybe page alignment or slab coalescing disabled on that kernel build. which kernel on d-4?
maya: d-4 kernel 5.14.0-rt27 (custom cloud image). Hosted is 5.19.0 and Private is 5.14 stock.
alex: driver differences? onprem had older nvidia driver that caused different mmap flags in our allocator previously. could be similar.
perf-bot: perf-alert: kvcache_eviction_rate dropped 93% on pool d-4 between 2026-03-02T09:00 and 2026-03-03T03:00 — linked dashboard https://redwood.ops/perf/alerts/kv-evict-d4
sam: did a quick grep in our runtime code: coalescer falls back to single-frame free when `madvise` returns ENOTSUP or if `mmap` flags include MAP_NORESERVE. maybe the cloud image changed default mm flags.
jin: can you capture `sysctl -a` and `cat /proc/sys/vm/*` on the failing host? also strace a small eviction to see `madvise`/`munmap` outcomes.
maya: grabbing now. also saw higher page-fault rates on d-4: `pgfault` ~480 vs hosted ~32 for same workload.
alex: sounds like kernel-level fragmentation: coalescing not working so eviction yields a lot of tiny spans that aren't usable for contiguous batches => allocator keeps growing.
sam: temporary mitigation: bump `kv.page_threshold` on Dedicated to 0.9 to force earlier eviction and reduce resident growth until we nail root cause. but that may raise latency for some requests.
jin: also try toggling `kv.coalesce.enabled=false` to see if path with different free logic behaves better (we added fallback in v1.23).
maya: tried coalesce=false — resident growth slowed but fragmentation metric still high. bumping threshold to 0.9 reduced steady-state by ~420MB but increased 95p latency by ~6ms.
alex: file an infra bug for d-4 image diff (kernel + glibc + nvidia). can we repro on a fresh dedicated with stock 5.19?
maya: provisioning a fresh dedicated with 5.19 now. will run the 20k token session.
perf-bot: note: related past incident 3067890123 showed similar eviction failures when kernel had CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM but different allocator paths. cross-ref: incident 3067890123.
jin: thanks. if repro on stock kernel, we root cause in runtime — otherwise push infra to rebuild the custom image. also capture `perf record` during eviction window so we can see where time and failures happen.
sam: quick triage checklist: 1) collect sysctl + vm stats 2) pmap + allocator dump 3) strace eviction 4) perf record 5) try threshold/coalesce toggles 6) repro on stock kernel
maya: copying checklist. will upload traces to the thread when done. @alex @jin @sam :eyes:
alex: thx — if you can't repro on stock kernel ping infra and we'll pause d-4 until image fixed. :thumbsup:
